instruction: Write a product description in the Spices, Inc. brand voice for the following blend.
input:
Name: Turkey Brine Seasoning
Category: Seasoning Blends
Cuisine: American
Characteristics: Holiday Spices and Seasonings, Turkey
Ingredients: kosher salt, brown sugar, white pepper, orange, garlic, black pepper, onion, rosemary, pink pepper, allspice, juniper, thyme, green pepper, basil, sage, oregano, bay leaves
output:
Turkey Brine Seasoning is an MSG-free, salty-sweet blend that’s made from turkey-friendly spices and herbs. It is also called turkey brine or turkey brine blend.
Brining, a salt-based method of preserving meat, has been in use around the globe for thousands of years. The earliest records of salt being used as a preservative was on fish. These records date back to the Sumerians, circa 3500 B.C. By 3000 B.C., Jewish settlements around the Dead Sea were using salt water to preserve meats that were more than just fish. In 200 B.C. the Romans learned the secrets of curing meat with salt from the Greeks, and also came to understand that nitrates in the salt gave their meat that pink hue. Fast-forwarding to a more modern era, in 1608 A.D Native Americans taught the people of Jamestown, Virginia their time-honored tradition of salting, smoking, and aging venison.
Turkey Brine Seasoning is popular with spice and olive oil shops, seasoning companies, butchers and meat processors, breweries, and bar and grill restaurants.

Flavor Profile
Turkey Brine Seasoning is a sweet-and-savory blend that tastes inherently salty, since it needs the salt to perform the chemistry of brining as well as to boost flavors. The rest of the flavor is rounded out by a menagerie of herbs, pungent aromatics, fruity peppercorn heat, and richness of allspice.

How to Use
For a medium-sized, 12-14 pound turkey, we recommend using 1 pound of Turkey Brine Seasoning. Add this to two gallons of brining liquid; you can use all water, or a combination of water and vegetable or chicken stock. Bring this to a boil, then remove from heat and allow to completely cool. When cool, put your turkey into a container, like a large stock pot or a brining bag. Pour the brine over the turkey and move it to a cool place. You can store it in your refrigerator, or in a cooler loaded with ice. If you use a cooler, check periodically to make sure the ice has not melted away. The turkey should sit in the brine at least 8 hours and up to 24 in your refrigerator or cooler.
An hour before you are ready to start cooking, remove your turkey from the brine. Discard the brine, rinse the turkey with cool water and then pat dry with paper towels. Let it come up to room temperature, and then prepare your turkey as you normally would for roasting. For the full recipe on the perfect Thanksgiving bird, check out our Classic Roast Turkey.
This brining blend also works well with chicken and pork chops, although we would not brine the chicken for more than four hours and the pork chops for more than two.

instruction: Write a product description in the Spices, Inc. brand voice for the following spice.
input:
Name: Organic Chipotle Flakes
Category: Chiles
Cuisine: Mexican
Characteristics: Chile Flakes, Chipotle Chile Powders and Seasonings, Classic Chili Spices, Dried Chile Peppers for Chili, New Products, Organic
output:
Organic Chipotle Flakes, Capsicum annuum, are hot chipotle morita chile flakes. They are also referred to as organic chipotle pepper flakes, organic smoky chipotle chili flakes, or organic chipotle chile flakes.
Chipotle morita chiles are made from jalapeno peppers that are fully ripened and smoked. Most jalapenos are picked while green but some are left to ripen to maturity on the vine. They are thick-walled chiles so once they are picked they are often smoked. Smoking preserves them more successfully than simply drying them, since the thicker walls take longer to dry and are more susceptible to microbial incursion.
Organic Chipotle Flakes are perfect for:
sauce, salsa, chile oil, chile paste, dip mix, jerky, and meal kit manufacturers;
Mexican, Latin American, BBQ, ramen, and Caribbean restaurants;
food trucks;
butchers;
meat processors;
seasoning companies; and
independent spice shops
One teaspoon of Organic Chipotle Flakes is roughly the equivalent of one whole Chipotle Morita Chile or one scant teaspoon of Organic Chipotle Morita Chile Powder.
Please visit our chile page to see the complete list of chiles, flakes, and powders we have available.

Flavor Profile
Organic Chipotle Flakes are fruity and smoky, with notes of berries and chocolate.

How To Use
Use Organic Chipotle Flakes anywhere you would normally used crushed red pepper flakes - on pizza, in salads, soups, stews and anywhere you want some authentic Mexican flavor. Spice up mushrooms with Champinones Al Ajillo Spanish Garlic Mushrooms. This flakes give Oaxacan Guacamole heat and depth. Stir into Caldo Tlalpeno (Chicken and Chipotle Soup), a healthy chicken soup loaded with vegetables. Organic Chipotle Flakes bring robust, peppery contrast to tart Roasted Salsa Verde.
Organic Chipotle Flakes are excellent with grilled or roasted meats, in salsas, sauces, and stews, soups, or pasta, and with cheese, rice, potatoes, and roasted vegetables.
Organic Chipotle Flakes pair well with tomato, garlic, onion, black pepper, fruit, thyme, cilantro, coriander, chocolate, nuts, and lime.

instruction: Write a product description in the Spices, Inc. brand voice for the following spice.
input:
Name: Organic California Minced Onion
Category: Staple Spices
Characteristics: Kosher, Onion, Organic, Umami, White Label Products
output:
Organic California Minced Onion, Allium cepa, may be known as organic minced onion, organic dried onions, or bulk organic minced onion. It is a member of the Allium family, and is a close relative of garlic, leeks, shallots, and bulbed flowers like the lily.

Our Organic Minced Onions are grown and processed in California. When they reach peak ripeness they are picked, dehydrated, and minced into easy to pour, easy to measure flakes that deliver the concentrated flavor of sweet onions without the tears.

Onions rank fourth in US vegetable consumption, behind heavy hitters like potatoes, tomatoes, and sweet corn. It is often purchased by those who manufacture organic snacks and snack mixes, jams, cheese, seasoning companies, spice shops and olive oil shops. It is also popular with food trucks, bagel and breakfast restaurants serving classic American fare.

If you want to learn more about onions, or see our selection of conventional or toasted onions, please visit our main onion page.

3 Tablespoons Organic California Minced Onion = 1 cup chopped onion.

Flavor Profile

Organic California Minced Onion has a sweet pungency and a rich umami flavor with a subtle, toasty finish.

How To Use

This minced version can be used in any recipe that calls for fresh onion. It is a convenient way to bring toasty onion flavor to savory recipes like soups, stews, casseroles and salads. Simmer some with ginger and garlic for rich and delicious Butter Chicken. Let it marinate overnight for savory New Mexican Pork Adovada. Add it to Spanish tapas-style meatballs called Albondigas. It also adds oniony goodness to dips, gravies, pan sauces, or Sichuan Hot Sauce. We suggest trying it in your favorite burger recipe or adding it to our Classic Burger with Cheese.

Onions are phenomenally cooperative with other herbs and spices. While they go with just about any savory food or cuisine imaginable, they pair exceptionally well with garlic, ginger, chiles, vinegar, tomatoes, tarragon, red wine, turmeric, and yogurt.

instruction: Write a product description in the Spices, Inc. brand voice for the following blend.
input:
Name: Celery Salt
Category: Salts
Characteristics: Salt Blends, White Label Products
Ingredients: sea salt, celery
output:
Combining celery seed and sea salt, our Celery Salt delivers the grassy, vegetal, pleasing bitterness of celery with the flavor-enhancing power of salt. Celery Salt is also known as bulk celery salt and is blended in our facility in small batches.

Celery Salt has long held a position on standard spice racks, but its origins are difficult to determine. According to some popular theories, the combination of celery’s naturally rich supply of nitrate with sodium was a particularly effective, and tasty, method for preserving meat. Another idea posits that celery seed, on its own, is a flavor enhancer, so combining it with salt helped to lower sodium intake before low-sodium diets were commonplace.

Celery Salt is popular with seafood, barbecue, and American restaurants, cafes, food trucks, delis, seasoning companies, manufacturers of sauces, gourmet nuts, dip mixes, and bloody mary mixes, as well as spice and olive oil shops.

Flavor Profile

The flavor of Celery Salt is pleasantly bitter, salty, and herbaceous.

How to Use

Celery Salt’s simple yet herby boost may surprise you. Add it to freshly sliced tomato and crusty bread for a quick and delicious summer lunch. Use it to draw out the flavors in delicate foods, like crab cakes or lobster rolls. Add it to just about any stew or soup you can imagine–stir it into Split Pea Soup,Chicken and Dumplings,Chicken and Sausage Jambalaya, or Hungarian Beef Stew. It goes beautifully in potato and macaroni salad, so put it on a traditional salad or toss it over the sweet potatoes and enjoy Roasted Sweet Potato with Smoky Chipotle Dressing.It adds a salty-herbaceous kick to freshly buttered corn on the cob. Let it boost your flavors in a classic southern Hoppin’ John, or use it to rim your glass when you make your next bloody Mary. Use as a finishing salt in Asian stir-fries, stir into vinaigrettes, and rub with black pepper over an entire chicken before roasting.

instruction: Write a product description in the Spices, Inc. brand voice for the following blend.
input:
Name: Satay Seasoning
Category: Seasoning Blends
Cuisine: Asian, Thai
Characteristics: Beef, Chicken Seasonings, Seafood, Vegetable
Ingredients: garlic, onion, sea salt, coriander, orange, turmeric, paprika, ginger, chipotle, lemongrass, cayenne
output:
Satay Seasoning is a bold, earthy, MSG-free seasoning blend that is loaded with spice and flavor. It is also known as sate seasoning, satay powder, sate spice, satay spice, satay seasoning mix, satay spice blend, or satay spice rub.
Satay is commonly associated with Thai food, but it’s generally thought that it originated on the island of Java, in Indonesia. This popular street food is comprised of grilled skewers of seasoned and barbecued meat or protein, accompanied by a flavorful sauce. It's usually made with chicken in the US but any kind of protein can become a satay, from beef to shrimp to tofu.
This product is frequently purchased by:
seasoning companies;
olive oil shops;
independent spice shops;
Chinese, American, and Mediterranean restaurants;
gastropubs; and
sauce, snack, dressing, and condiment manufacturers

Flavor Profile
Satay Seasoning is warm, tangy, and earthy, with elements of heat, smoke, and citrus.

How To Use
Use Satay Seasoning to make a satisfyingly savory Satay Chicken on the skewer. Or toss over jumbo shrimp and roll in eggroll wrappers to make Crispy Satay Shrimp Eggrolls. Serve both of these with creamy-crunchy Satay Peanut Sauce to enjoy the full satay experience. You can swap it in to season Spicy Thai Beef Salad, or stir with some sugar to make Smoked Ribs with an Asian twist.
Satay Seasoning is wonderful on chicken, pork, beef, seafood, or tofu. Use it in wraps and roasts, over grilled meats, with vegetables, in marinades, dressings, or in soups and stews.

instruction: Write a product description in the Spices, Inc. brand voice for the following spice.
input:
Name: Brown Mustard Seeds
Category: Staple Spices
Characteristics: Kosher, Umami
output:
Brown mustard seeds, Brassica juncea, also sometimes known as Indian mustard seeds, brown mustard seed, bulk mustard, whole brown mustard seeds or Indian mustard, are an important spice in many regional cuisines. These seeds contain .8-3.0% of the pungent volatile oil by weight, and approximately 30% oil overall.
Brown mustard seeds are hotter than yellow mustard seeds, but not quite as pungent as black seeds.&
These seeds are frequently purchased by:
American and seafood restaurants;
brewpubs;
gastro pubs;
independent spice shops;
delis; and
companies that manufacture sauces, condiments, mustard and pretzels
We also carry Yellow Mustard Seed, Black Mustard Seed, Ground Yellow Mustard, Brown Mustard Powder, Hot Mustard Powder, and Organic Ground Yellow Mustard.

Flavor Profile
Brown mustard seeds have a sharp, earthy, and pungent flavor, with medium heat. Dry roasting mustard seeds will help bring out their aroma and flavor.

How To Use
Brown mustard seeds are hotter and smaller than the yellow seeds, and are used in traditional African and Asian recipes. For a traditional Indian dish, consider a classic Mango Chutney. Or stir into an African-style Chicken Tagine. Use brown mustard in spice rubs and marinades for grilling. Try brown mustard seeds in place of yellow in your next pickle brine. Make your own German Style Mustard to serve with Soft Pretzels for an Oktoberfest treat.
Brown mustard works especially well in Indian curry dishes when partnered with asafoetida, coriander, cumin, curry leaf and fennel. You'll also find that they work well when combined with bay, chili powder, dill, fenugreek, garlic, honey, nigella, parsley, pepper, tarragon and turmeric.

instruction: Write a product description in the Spices, Inc. brand voice for the following blend.
input:
Name: Pacific Northwest Seafood Seasoning
Category: Seasoning Blends
Cuisine: American
Characteristics: Seafood, White Label Products
Ingredients: garlic, onion, paprika, black pepper, dill, celery, parsley, sea salt, lemon
output:
Pacific Northwest Seafood Seasoning is also known as northwest seafood or seafood seasoning. It is MSG free.
The Pacific Northwest (PNW) is home to an enormous wealth of seafood like salmon, halibut, mussels, Dungeness crab, fresh shucked oysters, giant geoducks (a species of very large, edible saltwater clams) and succulent sweet spot prawns. Modern chefs celebrate the diversity of this region by combining the cornucopia of regional ingredients with modern cooking techniques for a contemporary take on local cuisine that’s innovative and fresh, with an eye toward sustainability in practice.
Pacific Northwest Seafood Seasoning is popular with seasoning companies; independent spice shops; olive oil shops; manufacturers of coffee and tea; American restaurants; and catering companies.

Flavor Profile
Pacific Northwest Seafood Seasoning is fragrant, warm, herbaceous, and bright.

How To Use
Our Pacific Northwest Seafood Seasoning is good on just about anything that comes out of the water. Use it to season Parmesan-Crusted Fish with Asparagus. Add to the steaming liquid for mussels for a rich broth or choose it as your flavor base for Crab and Corn Chowder. Add to the sauteeing onions for a boost of flavor in Shrimp and Crabmeat Etouffee. Mix into the breading when making fried calamari.
This blend is also good rubbed into chicken cacciatore or in Slow Cooker Pulled Pork. Vegetarians can enjoy this blend in a Vegetable Paella. Mix with red wine vinegar and oil for a zesty vinaigrette.
This blend can be used to make broth, breading, stews, soups, chowder, risotto, chicken, pork, vegetarian entrees, or salad dressing.

instruction: Write a product description in the Spices, Inc. brand voice for the following spice.
input:
Name: Organic Black Peppercorns 
Characteristics: Organic, Pepper, Peppercorns, White Label Products
output:
Organic Black Peppercorns, Piper nigrum, are also known as organic peppercorns, organic whole peppercorns, organic black peppercorns, organic pepper corns, and organic peppercorn.
Our Organic Black Peppercorns contain between 1-2.5% essential oil.
Pepper is a fruiting vine in the family Piperaceae and is native to the Malabar region of southern India. When the fruit is fully mature, it is approximately 2/10" in diameter, dark red, and contains a single seed. Black, green, and white peppercorns are all products of the same vine, harvested and processed at different points in its maturity to create these varieties. You can browse the different peppercorns on our main peppercorn page.
Organic Black Peppercorns are popular with salt, coffee, tea, and vinegar manufacturers; spice shops; and brewpubs, Mediterranean, and Mexican restaurants.
1 teaspoon of Organic Black Peppercorns = 1 ¼ teaspoon ground black pepper.

Flavor Profile
Organic Black Peppercorns produce a distinctly spicy flavor. They are slightly hot and biting with notes of pine and just a hint of sweetness.

How To Use
Organic Black Peppercorns are ubiquitous in kitchens across the country. Use them in any recipe that calls for pepper. They are best when ground to the coarseness or fineness called for in a recipe right before use.
Black pepper goes well with basil, beef, cilantro, coconut milk, creamy sauces, eggs, fermented soybeans, garlic, ginger, lemon, pork, red wine, seafood, soy sauce, and vegetables. It also pairs nicely with basil, cardamom, cinnamon, cloves, coriander, cumin, garlic, ginger, nutmeg, parsley, rosemary, thyme and turmeric.

instruction: Write a product description in the Spices, Inc. brand voice for the following spice.
input:
Name: Organic Ground Cloves
Category: Baking
Characteristics: Organic, White Label Products
output:
Organic Ground Cloves,Syzygium aromaticum, are also known as organic bulk ground cloves. Cloves are a pungent spice, delivering a minimum of 10% essential oil by weight.
Cloves are the unopened buds of an Indonesian evergreen tree. The buds turn red right before they open, which is when they are harvested and dried. The word “clove” comes from the Latin clavus, or nail, and European colonizers named them so because of their spiky appearance.
Organic Ground Cloves are popular with seasoning companies; honey, sauce, and baked goods manufacturers; independent spice shops; Mexican and African restaurants; delis; and breweries.
We also have conventional Ground Cloves and Whole Cloves available.

Flavor Profile
Organic Ground Cloves are peppery, woodsy, and intensely warm, with a mild, numbing quality.

How To Use
Organic Ground Cloves are used in popular soups such as red lentil soup and Spicy Pumpkin Soup. Substitute Organic Ground Cloves into Apple Pie Fries or Healthy Carrot Cake Squares. Organic Ground Cloves can spice up Cincinnati Skyline Chili and Birria – Mexican Beef Stew, the latter of which can even be shredded into tacos. Use this when making an organic DIY Dry Rib Rub.
Organic Ground Cloves are delicious in savory or sweet pies and puddings, dessert cakes, candies, or cookies. Add to gravies, cranberry sauce, roasts, applesauce, tea, cider, BBQ sauce, chili, soups, stews, and braises.
Organic Ground Cloves pair well with cinnamon, allspice, vanilla, onion, citrus peel, star anise, basil, pork, ham, beef, turkey, peppercorns, oranges, carrots, apples, beets, and pumpkin.

instruction: Write a product description in the Spices, Inc. brand voice for the following blend.
input:
Name: Maple Sausage Seasoning
Category: Seasoning Blends
Cuisine: American
Characteristics: Sausage Seasonings, White Label Products
Ingredients: fennel, sugar, kosher salt, black pepper, maple, fenugreek, onion, coriander, nutmeg, cayenne
output:
Maple Sausage Seasoning is a sweet and spicy, MSG-free seasoning blend. It is also referred to as maple breakfast sausage seasoning, maple sausage spices, and sweet maple sausage blend.
While sausage has been enjoyed around the globe for thousands of years, maple-flavored sausage is most likely an American creation. With the introduction of maple sap and syrup into their diet, North American settlers began choosing maple as a sweetener in the 1800s. The first commercial maple-focused seasonings appeared on shelves in the early part of the 1900s, and saw an explosion in popularity in the 1950s and 1960s.
Maple Sausage Seasoning is sought after by:
sausage, meal kit, and subscription manufacturers;
Italian, barbeque, and breakfast restaurants;
cafes;
independent spice shops; and
seasoning companies

Flavor Profile
Maple Sausage Seasoning is sweet, resinous, spicy, and maple-y, with herbaceous fennel and bold pops of black pepper and salt.

How To Use
Mix Maple Sausage Seasoning into ground pork and enjoy Maple Sausage with Sweet Potato Waffle. Make a Maple Roasted Chicken Salad with some seasoned chicken and acorn squash for a hearty, filling fall salad. Blend into beef or turkey and make Glazed Meatballs over Soba Noodles. Swap it into Baked Hash Browns or Chicken and Sausage Jambalaya.
When making sausage, we recommend 1 1/2-2 Tablespoons of Maple Sausage Seasoning per pound of meat, since sausage tends to be more intensely seasoned that other dishes.
This blend is delicious when made into loose or cased sausages. It pairs with pork, chicken, turkey, duck, tofu, seitan, or beef. Use on roasted winter squash, beets, potatoes and sweet potatoes, carrots, and zucchini. Top sourdough or other rustic crackers and breads, flatbreads, pretzels, or gourmet pizza.

instruction: Write a product description in the Spices, Inc. brand voice for the following blend.
input:
Name: Adobo Lime Rub 
Category: Seasoning Blends
Cuisine: Caribbean, Mexican
Characteristics: BBQ Rubs and Grill Seasonings, Chicken Seasonings, Citrus Seasoning Blends, Olive Oil Shop Top 50 Seasonings, Seafood, Sugar Free, Vegetable, White Label Products
Ingredients: sea salt, cumin, fennel, garlic, lime (rice maltodextrin, lime juice concentrate), black pepper, coriander, oregano, thyme, rosemary
output:
Adobo Lime Rub is well-balanced and lively, with plenty of refreshing lime balanced out by fragrant herbs and aromatics. Our Adobo Lime Rub is also sometimes called adobo lime or lime adobo rub.

Before refrigeration was commonplace, people had to develop ways to preserve food safely; if that preservation method could infuse food with flavor, so much the better for it. Enter adobo. Taken from the Spanish word adobar, “to marinate”, adobo was originally a means to preserve food in salt and vinegar or wine, and seasoning spices, creating dishes that were packed with flavor and reflective of local ingredients.

Adobo Lime Rub is a favorite with seasoning companies, olive oil shops, spice shops, butchers, American and Mediterranean restaurants and those who manufacturer jams or gourmet jams.

Flavor Profile

Citrusy, earthy, and savory with garlic and anise-like undertones.

How to Use

We love this rub on chicken and lighter seafood like tilapia and salmon. Use Adobo Lime Rub to season Zesty Grilled Jalapeno Chicken for a spicy supper. Perk up your side dish with Grilled Broccoli in Adobo Lime Marinade. Swap it into Crispy Fish Tacos and serve them in tortillas with a crisp cabbage slaw. Toss seared plantains in Adobo Lime Rub and mash for a classic Caribbean mofongo. Whip up some Pineapple Cilantro Dressing to serve over the Al Pastor Kebob Salad Bowl.

instruction: Write a product description in the Spices, Inc. brand voice for the following spice.
input:
Name: Granulated Brown Sugar
Category: Baking
Characteristics: White Label Products
output:
Granulated Brown Sugar is an easy-to-pour version of the traditional brown sugar many home cooks have come to love over time. It is also known as bulk brown sugar, brown sugar, granulated brown sugar, and brown granulated sugar.
Our Granulated Brown Sugar is made through co-crystallization, a process where the sugar and molasses are blended as syrups and allowed to cool together, forming the final product.
Granulated Brown Sugar is popular with seasoning companies, manufacturers of coffee, tea, sauces, and jams, Mexican, barbecue, and hotel restaurants, food trucks, distillers, and spice shops.

Flavor Profile
Granulated Brown Sugar is a dryer brown sugar with a gentler molasses flavor.

How to Use
Granulated Brown Sugar functions more like white sugar than regular brown sugar in baking, so use it as a replacement for light brown sugar. Granulated Brown Sugar is perfect to use in a variety of baked goods like these light and tasty Vanilla Bean Cookies and moist Healthy Carrot Cake Squares. It gives homemade Ketchup a savory sweetness and tames the heat in these Korean Chicken Wings.

instruction: Write a product description in the Spices, Inc. brand voice for the following spice.
input:
Name: New Mexico Lumbre Chile Powder
Category: Chiles
Characteristics: Chile Powders, White Label Products
output:
New Mexico Lumbre Chile Powder, Capsicum annuum, is a hot powder that measures approximately 35,000 Scoville Heat Units (SHU). The Lumbre is the equivalent of a cayenne or tabasco pepper. Once you get behind the up-front heat of the New Mexico Lumbre Chile Powder, you’ll find this pepper has a grassy sweetness, tempered with an earthy undertone that provides a complex flavor profile. Lumbre means “fire” in Mexican slang, but this pepper, with its classic New Mexican flavor below the fire, has so much more to offer than the pleasant burn of a capsaicin-laced pepper.

The Lumbre chile was developed by Jim Lytle and Faron Lytle, a father-son team of chile farmers and members of the Franzoy family, the chile farming dynasty that helped raise the valley around Hatch, New Mexico into an elite chile-growing region. They developed it after 9 years of work, with a minimum five-year trial period to establish its characteristic stability, simply because they wanted to offer a hotter variety of pepper to their chile fans.

Tips From Our Kitchen

Coat party cheese balls with chopped pine nuts and a sprinkling of our New Mexico Lumbre Chile Powder. For extra bang, toss bacon in Lumbre chile powder and bake until crisp; crumble the bacon and add that to the cheese coating. Toss pasta with olive oil, New Mexico Lumbre Chile Powder, lime zest, cotija cheese and some chopped scallions for a New Mexican twist on pasta. Infuse your favorite tequila with Lumbre powder and enjoy a spicy margarita.
